canh-rau-ngot-nau-tom.name: Vietnamese sweet leaf soup with prawns
aliases: Sweet leaf and fresh prawn soup
Vietnamese sweet leaf soup with river shrimp
canh-rau-ngot-nau-tom.description: Gently bruised rau ngót leaves and fresh prawns make a clear, mildly sweet soup for an everyday Vietnamese family meal. Bếp Việt standardizes the amounts for four and keeps the cooking brief so the leaves stay green.
canh-rau-ngot-nau-tom.finished_dish: The leaves are just tender and still green; sweet prawns sit in a clear, delicate broth seasoned lightly with fish sauce and pepper.
canh-rau-ngot-nau-tom.serving: Serve hot with chopped scallion and pepper. Pair with steamed rice and a braised or glazed dish.
tips: Bruise the leaves only lightly; excessive rubbing or boiling can cloud the broth and dull the green color.
Coarsely pound or mince small prawns; dice larger ones for easier eating.
Add fish sauce gradually at the end to preserve the natural sweetness of the greens and prawns.
search_terms: Vietnamese sweet leaf soup with prawns
canh-rau-ngot-nau-tom.image_alt: A bowl of green rau ngót soup with fresh prawns in a light broth, garnished with scallion and pepper; original Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
canh-rau-ngot-nau-tom.time_note: About 27 minutes, including picking the leaves, preparing the prawns and a quick simmer.

ingredients.name: Rau ngót (Vietnamese sweet leaf)
ingredients.notes: Pick tender leaves, wash and gently bruise.

ingredients.name: Peeled river prawns
ingredients.notes: Devein; coarsely mince or pound.

ingredients.name: Shallot
ingredients.notes: Peel and finely mince.

ingredients.name: Scallion
ingredients.notes: Wash and chop for garnish.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Add more if you prefer a lighter soup.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Season after the greens are just tender.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Lightly season the prawns and soup.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Use a little with the prawns and the rest to finish.

preparation_steps: Pick off tough stems, wash the rau ngót and gently bruise the leaves. Peel and devein the prawns, then coarsely mince or pound them; season with a little salt and pepper.
cooking_steps: Bring the water to a boil. Add the prawns in small portions, stir to separate them and skim once the broth returns to a boil.
Lower to medium heat, add the rau ngót and simmer for 2–3 minutes after the broth returns to a boil, until the leaves are just tender and still green.
Season with fish sauce and the remaining salt. Turn off the heat, add scallion and pepper, and serve hot.
canh-rau-ngot-nau-tom.serving_basis: One light soup pot for four, served with rice and a savory main dish.

ga-xao-sa-ot.name: Lemongrass and chili chicken stir-fry
aliases: Chicken stir-fried with lemongrass and chili
ga-xao-sa-ot.description: Bite-size chicken thigh is marinated with lemongrass, garlic and fish sauce, then quickly stir-fried over high heat. Sliced lemongrass, lime leaf and chili add fragrance to this familiar Vietnamese rice dish.
ga-xao-sa-ot.finished_dish: The chicken is tender and lightly browned, coated in seasoning, with fragrant lemongrass, gentle chili heat and a hint of lime leaf.
ga-xao-sa-ot.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice. Adjust the chili to taste; use seeded mild red pepper when cooking for children.
tips: Cut the chicken evenly and pat it dry so it seasons well.
Stir-fry in a single layer over high heat; cook in two batches if the pan is small.
Add the lime leaf near the end to preserve its aroma.
ga-xao-sa-ot.image_alt: A plate of golden lemongrass and chili chicken with sliced lemongrass, red chili and lime leaf; original Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
ga-xao-sa-ot.time_note: About 47 minutes, including a 15-minute marinade and a quick stir-fry.

ingredients.name: Boneless chicken thigh
ingredients.notes: Remove the skin if you prefer a lighter dish; cut into bite-size pieces.

ingredients.name: Lemongrass
ingredients.notes: Slice some stalks and finely mince the rest.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Red chili
ingredients.notes: Seed or reduce the amount for less heat.

ingredients.name: Lime leaves
ingredients.notes: Wash and finely shred.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Use part of it in the marinade.

ingredients.name: Oyster sauce
ingredients.notes: Reduce for a lighter flavor.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Balance the saltiness of the fish sauce.

ingredients.name: Ground pepper
ingredients.notes: Use in the marinade and to finish.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For frying the aromatics and chicken.

ingredients.name: Toasted sesame seeds
ingredients.notes: Sprinkle at the end; optional.

preparation_steps: Pat the chicken dry and cut it into bite-size strips. Slice some lemongrass and mince the rest; mince the garlic, slice the chili and shred the lime leaves.
Combine the chicken with fish sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, pepper, half the minced lemongrass and half the garlic. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for 15 minutes.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil and fry the sliced lemongrass until fragrant and lightly golden; remove it. Add the remaining minced garlic and lemongrass and stir until aromatic.
Add the chicken to the hot pan in a moderate layer and stir-fry over high heat until browned and thoroughly cooked, stirring so it does not scorch.
Add the chili, reserved lemongrass and lime leaf. Taste and adjust, stir for about one minute, then turn off the heat. Finish with sesame and serve hot.
ga-xao-sa-ot.serving_basis: One fragrant chicken stir-fry for four, served with steamed rice.

so-long-xao-sa-ot.name: Cockles stir-fried with lemongrass and chili
aliases: Cockles with lemongrass, garlic and chili
so-long-xao-sa-ot.description: Live cockles are soaked to release grit, briefly boiled until they open, then shelled and quickly stir-fried with lemongrass, garlic and chili. The short stir-fry preserves their natural sweetness and works as a hot rice dish or shared snack.
so-long-xao-sa-ot.finished_dish: The cockle meat is tender and lightly coated in seasoning, with fragrant lemongrass, golden garlic and adjustable chili heat.
so-long-xao-sa-ot.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice. Choose live shellfish, wash thoroughly and discard any that smell off or remain closed after boiling.
tips: Soak the cockles for about an hour in rice-rinse water or lightly salted water, then scrub them well.
Boil only until the shells open, remove the meat and avoid over-stir-frying it.
Reduce the fish sauce and taste before adding salt if the cockles are naturally briny.
so-long-xao-sa-ot.image_alt: A plate of shelled cockle meat stir-fried with lemongrass, garlic and red chili; original Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
so-long-xao-sa-ot.time_note: About 117 minutes using a 90-minute soak; soak the cockles for 1?2 hours to release sand, while the stir-fry itself is quick.

ingredients.name: Live cockles in shells
ingredients.notes: Choose tightly closed shells; remove the meat after boiling.

ingredients.name: Rice-rinse water or lightly salted water
ingredients.notes: For soaking to release grit; do not use it for cooking.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Dissolve in water if rice-rinse water is unavailable.

ingredients.name: Lemongrass
ingredients.notes: Remove tough outer layers; mince or thinly slice.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Red chili
ingredients.notes: Slice; reduce for mild heat.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For frying the aromatics.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Add gradually depending on the brininess of the cockles.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Balance salt and chili.

ingredients.name: Seasoning powder
ingredients.notes: Use a small amount; salt may be used instead.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Sprinkle after cooking.

preparation_steps: Soak the cockles in rice-rinse water or lightly salted water for 1?2 hours. Scrub the shells under running water; discard dead, cracked or unpleasant-smelling shellfish.

Mince the lemongrass and garlic and slice the chili. Bring a pot of water to a boil, add the cockles and boil for about three minutes until they open. Cool slightly, remove the meat and discard the shells and any cockles that did not open.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil in a pan, fry the garlic until fragrant, then add the lemongrass and cook until aromatic.
Add the cockle meat and stir-fry quickly over high heat. Season with fish sauce, sugar and seasoning powder; cook for 3–4 minutes until just firm and coated.
Add the chili and stir for about one minute. Turn off the heat, finish with pepper, taste and serve hot.
so-long-xao-sa-ot.serving_basis: One cockle stir-fry for four; the purchase weight includes shells.

canh-bap-cai-cuon-thit.name: Vietnamese cabbage-roll pork soup
aliases: Vietnamese cabbage rolls with minced pork soup
canh-bap-cai-cuon-thit.description: Tender cabbage leaves wrap a pork and wood-ear filling, then simmer gently in a light broth with carrot. This tidy, comforting soup is easy to pair with rice and other everyday dishes.
canh-bap-cai-cuon-thit.finished_dish: The cabbage rolls are soft but hold their shape; the pork filling is juicy and cooked through, with a delicate broth scented with scallion and cilantro.
canh-bap-cai-cuon-thit.serving: Ladle a few rolls and hot broth into each bowl. Serve with steamed rice and a savory dish that is not too soupy.
tips: Blanch the leaves only until pliable; overcooked leaves tear or become mushy.
Tie each roll with a blanched scallion and place the seam side down in the pot.
Simmer gently until the center of the filling is fully cooked; a vigorous boil can break the rolls.
canh-bap-cai-cuon-thit.image_alt: A bowl of Vietnamese cabbage rolls filled with pork and tied with scallion, with carrot in clear broth; original Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
canh-bap-cai-cuon-thit.time_note: About 55 minutes, including a 10-minute wood-ear soak, rolling and simmering.

ingredients.name: Cabbage
ingredients.notes: Choose large intact leaves for rolling; slice any trimmings for the soup.

ingredients.name: Ground pork
ingredients.notes: A little fat helps keep the filling moist.

ingredients.name: Dried wood-ear mushrooms
ingredients.notes: Soak until soft, rinse and mince.

ingredients.name: Carrot
ingredients.notes: Peel and cut into rounds or small pieces.

ingredients.name: Shallot
ingredients.notes: Peel and finely mince.

ingredients.name: Scallion
ingredients.notes: Blanch long green sections for tying; chop the rest.

ingredients.name: Cilantro
ingredients.notes: Wash and chop for garnish.

ingredients.name: Pork stock or water
ingredients.notes: Use prepared stock or plain water.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: Fry the shallot if cooking with water.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Season the filling and broth.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Season the broth gradually.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Mix into the filling and use lightly to finish.

preparation_steps: Soak the wood-ear mushrooms in warm water for 10 minutes, rinse and mince. Separate eight intact cabbage leaves, wash and blanch until pliable. Blanch long scallion greens for tying.
Mix the ground pork with wood ear, shallot, some fish sauce and pepper. Divide into eight portions, place each on a cabbage leaf, fold the sides, roll and tie gently with scallion.
cooking_steps: Bring the stock to a gentle boil. If using water, first fry the shallot in oil until fragrant, then add the water. Add the carrot and cook for about three minutes.
Arrange the cabbage rolls seam-side down. Lower to a gentle simmer, partially cover and cook for about 15–17 minutes until the pork filling is thoroughly cooked; skim the surface for a clear broth.
Season with fish sauce and salt. Turn off the heat, add chopped scallion and cilantro, and ladle carefully to keep the rolls intact.
canh-bap-cai-cuon-thit.serving_basis: A pot of soup with about eight pork-filled cabbage rolls for four people.

bo-xao-hoa-thien-ly.name: Beef stir-fried with Tonkin jasmine flowers
aliases: Vietnamese beef and Tonkin jasmine stir-fry
Beef stir-fried with bông thiên lý and cracklings
bo-xao-hoa-thien-ly.description: Thinly sliced beef is quickly stir-fried with fresh clusters of thiên lý flowers, a familiar Vietnamese garden ingredient. Bếp Việt adds a small amount of cracklings as an optional family-style variation noted in the references.
bo-xao-hoa-thien-ly.finished_dish: The beef is tender, the flowers remain green and lightly crisp, and a few cracklings add gentle savory richness.
bo-xao-hoa-thien-ly.serving: Serve immediately with steamed rice. Avoid holding the stir-fry, as the flowers lose color and the beef can toughen.
tips: Slice the beef across the grain and marinate briefly; sear it in small batches over high heat.
Trim tough stems, rinse the flowers gently and dry them well to keep the stir-fry from becoming watery.
Return the beef and cracklings only at the end and toss briefly to keep the flowers green and the meat tender.
bo-xao-hoa-thien-ly.image_alt: A plate of beef stir-fried with green thiên lý flower clusters, crisp golden cracklings and garlic; original Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
bo-xao-hoa-thien-ly.time_note: About 45 minutes, including a 15-minute beef marinade and quick stir-frying in batches.

ingredients.name: Beef sirloin or shank
ingredients.notes: Slice thinly across the grain.

ingredients.name: Thiên lý flower clusters
ingredients.notes: Trim tough stems, rinse gently and drain well.

ingredients.name: Pork fat
ingredients.notes: Dice and render into crisp cracklings; omit and use cooking oil for a lighter version.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Oyster sauce
ingredients.notes: Use to marinate the beef.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Season the flowers and adjust at the end.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Balance the seasoning.

ingredients.name: Seasoning powder
ingredients.notes: Use a small amount; optional.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Use in the marinade and to finish.

preparation_steps: Pat the beef dry and slice thinly across the grain. Mix with oyster sauce, sugar, a little fish sauce, pepper and half the garlic; cover and marinate in the refrigerator for 15 minutes.
Pick through the thiên lý flowers, remove tough stems and wilted buds, rinse gently and drain thoroughly. Dice the pork fat.
cooking_steps: Start the pork fat in a cool pan and render over medium heat until the fat is released and the cracklings are golden and crisp. Remove the cracklings and keep a little rendered fat in the pan.
Raise the heat, fry the remaining garlic and quickly sear the beef in batches until just browned; transfer it to a plate so it does not toughen.

Use the same pan to stir-fry the flowers for 2–3 minutes. Season with the remaining fish sauce and seasoning powder. When just tender, return the beef and cracklings, toss for about 30 seconds and turn off the heat.
bo-xao-hoa-thien-ly.serving_basis: One hot beef and flower stir-fry for four, served with rice.
